lead: The settlement that gives its name to the district and the old municipality, from fields and farmhouses to a neighbourhood of blocks in the 1950s.
text: It gives its name to the district and to the old municipality of Sant Martí de Provençals, independent until 1897. Until the 1950s it was mostly farmland, with farmhouses (masies) such as Can Planas, Ca l'Arnó, Can Riera and Can Cadena and a church, and in the late 19th century painters such as Nonell, Mir and Pichot came to paint its fields. In the former Pere Calafell school, at Carrer d'Andrade, 184, the City Council renovated part of the building for the municipal nursery school L'Esquitx, with 85 places and an investment of 3.86 million euros.

The present-day neighbourhood arose from the waves of migration of the 1950s: the first housing groups, on both sides of Carrer de Guipúscoa, were promoted by the Caixa de Pensions and the Obra Sindical del Hogar, and a partial plan of 1958 sped up the construction of large blocks. Facilities and services were lacking, and community campaigning and the democratisation of institutions gradually filled the gaps, with the arrival of the metro and the redevelopment of the Rambla de Guipúscoa. With 27,035 inhabitants in 0.73 km² and 36,832 inhabitants/km², it is a dense neighbourhood, with average prices of 3,304 €/m² for sale and 1,011 €/month for rent, below those of Poblenou and La Vila Olímpica. If you are selling, the average sale price is 20% below the Sant Martí average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 264,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Sant Martí (8th of 10 by price). If you are investing, the average rent is 8% below the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Blocks of flats built from the 1950s onwards, in an inland neighbourhood of the district.
places: Església de Sant Martí de Provençals
